title: MV Smarter pathfinding for chasing events

posts.author: muffinswords
posts.body:
I feel like this is one that has been done before, but I'm coming up empty on a cursory look through the internet.
I'm looking for a plugin that will essentially make events chasing or following the player smarter. Right now there's a few issues:
-getting stuck on events or tiles
-getting confused and stuck about cliffs, mazes, various walls
-getting confused or stuck if too far away period
-trying to reach the player by simply getting closer to the player, for example on a cliff above the player's position (technically next to the player but on a whole different level of the map), as opposed to taking the ACTUAL route they need to reach the player
I feel like players will complain if my implementation is off so I want it to be as polished as I can. Are there any options available that achieve an intelligent pathfinding?
I'm already using Yanfly's Move Route Core, and it's very useful, but its pathfinding for chasing events is still "dumb." I've also tried Shaz's Smart Pathfinding with the same results.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Pretty much every pathfinding plugin will use A*, and it's also what RPG Maker uses for its findDirectionTo function which is called when you click the screen and the player pathfinds to that tile.
To do the fancy stuff you want taking layers, moving events, etc into account, well, that's something you will likely need to write in extra conditional statements yourself.
It's going to be more complicated and processor intensive than you think, because if the other events are moving it will have to be constantly calculating a new route to go around them, meaning it has to sample every tile in an x tile radius until it hits its target. The longer it takes to find a clear path, or the more often it needs to recalculate, the more lag you'll get.
Play around with this tool and you'll see what's happening when you tell an event to pathfind
PathFinding.js
The event has to sample all those green tiles to find a path, except now you're adding in extra dynamic walls (moving events) whose position change every frame

posts.body: just a thought to prevent "trapping".  Have the program calculate a larger pattern every 5 to 10 cycles, and if detected, calculate a path out of the pocket zone.  This wouldn't prevent it from going back in, but at least it wouldn't get trapped there.  The condition for knowing if it is trapped... (X and Y coordinates over time did not change by more than X.  This would kick it to long range detection.  If the event is actually trapped, it would be no harm, no foul... and use up less resources than a constant check.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
When a character is pathfinding (e.g. the player via touch input) the core engine calls
findDirectionTo
every step, which uses an A* algorithm to (re)find a path, up to the search limit, and returns the direction for the next step along that path. Yanfly's and Shaz's plugins simply use this built-in pathfinding, because why not?
Well, the default search limit of 12 tiles is tuned to the standard 17x13 tiles per screen, since it's only designed for player touch movement. That does mean it will fail over larger distances for certain configurations of obstacles. As you can see from the link/screenshot AquaEcho shared, the impact of increasing the search limit is very dependent on the map layout: narrow corridors will cause minimal issues, while open-plan maps will be much more CPU-hungry.
In terms of failure: A* with no search limit is mathematically guaranteed to find a path if one exists. So if effectively removing the search limit (e.g.
9999
, or
Infinity
) does not help, it's something else (or there is a 9-year-old flaw in
findDirectionTo
). Ideas:
If it locks up completely with a high search limit then try turning off any plugins you're using in the Plugin Manager (right-click -> Turn OFF) to see if that helps. E.g. a plugin that adds mechanical map layers may change the passability of a tile based on the character's current layer:
findDirectionTo
doesn't account for layers by default, so that plugin (or an extension for it) would have to patch the pathfinder appropriately to avoid related bugs. Bugs like, say, pathing from tile A (lower layer) to tile B (upper layer) when the target XY is only accessible on the lower layer: the path returns to A, but then is back where it started - a loop.
If it results in pathing that stops unexpectedly (or never!), and/or does a lot of moving back and forth, that may be due to passability changes during the movement. If, say, a shortcut is periodically opening and closing, the pathfinder might alternate between "let's take the shortcut" and "looks like we have to go the long way around". A similar thing can happen with a wandering NPC temporarily blocking a hallway.
Accounting for changes over time means that you basically have to "path" in some way for all agents in the area just to move one of them, e.g. LPA* or (more practically) D* Lite.
